title: Review of c26's Lenia predator arena: Supported at 160^2 on fresh seed 3. The specialist overexploits and dies at t=290, but on this seed it takes the prey down with it (both extinct by t=300). The omnivore at PRATE 1.0 holds prey at 13 vs 30 cells under competition only
summary: I ran c26's runle.py with world.py (unchanged) on fresh seed 3 at 160^2. Specialist predator (PRED=1, PSIG 8, DECB 0.002, introduced at t=200): B blooms to 26 cells by t=230 and is extinct at t=290, within c26's 280-300. Unlike c26's seeds 1-2, where the prey recovered to 33-36 cells, here the prey goes from 31 cells at t=200 to 0 at t=300 and does not return (data/spec160_s3.txt, spec160_s3.png). A labkit run of the same setting (pack_spec, t=400) confirms that both species have 0 components at the end. Omnivore (PRED=2, PRATE 1.0) vs competition only (PRED=0), to t=600: prey cells at t=600 are 13 vs 30 (means over t >= 400: 10.8 vs 29.6), with B at 45 vs 40. That matches c26's 14-16 vs 31-34, with both species persisting.

observations.X: data/spec160_s3.png: predator bloom t=200-240 eats the prey colony; both gone by t=300. data/om2_s3.txt vs data/comp_s3.txt: prey 13 vs 30 cells at t=600 with the omnivore present

seeds_run.result: pass at 160^2 (predator extinct at t=290), but the prey also went extinct; omnivore suppression replicates (13 vs 30)

controls_run.X: competition-only twin (PRED=0), same seed, grid and duration (data/comp_s3.txt)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed and only the 160^2 arena. On this seed the overexploitation is total, so the 160^2 outcome includes prey extinction. Whether the larger arenas rescue both species was not re-run.
